questions.prompt: Where do you go with your class to look at old and beautiful objects?
questions.explanation: Old and beautiful objects are kept in a museum. You watch a film at the cinema, you eat at a restaurant, and you look at animals at the zoo.

questions.prompt: Complete: "My brother dislikes ___ . He never goes to the shops with us."
questions.explanation: Dislike belongs to the same family as like, enjoy and hate, so the activity that follows it takes the -ing form: my brother dislikes shopping. The forms "shop", "shops" and "to shop" are the bare verb, the he/she/it form and the infinitive, and none of them can follow dislike.

questions.prompt: Complete both blanks: "I do my homework ___ the afternoon and I watch TV ___ the evening."
questions.explanation: The afternoon and the evening are both parts of the day, with no day named beside them, so both blanks take in. The preposition on would be right only if a day appeared, as in on Sunday afternoon.

questions.prompt: Complete both blanks: "I like gardening ___ I hate shopping, ___ the shops are always full."
questions.explanation: Liking gardening and hating shopping are two different ideas, so but joins them, and the last part explains why the shops are not pleasant, so because opens it. Starting with because would make hating shopping the reason for liking gardening, and ending with and or with but would leave the explanation without its reason word.

questions.prompt: Your team needs one more player and you want Sarra in it. Which question invites her?

options.text: Do you like to join our team?
Would you like join our team?
Would you like joining our team?
Would you like to join our team?

questions.explanation: An invitation is Would you like + to + verb: Would you like to join our team? The version with "Do you like" asks about a habit, not about today, "Would you like join" drops the word to, and "Would you like joining" borrows the -ing form that belongs after How about.

questions.prompt: Read: "Nadia goes to the cinema every Friday. Her brother goes one time a year." Which sentence describes them?

options.text: Nadia always goes to the cinema on Friday, and her brother sometimes goes.
Nadia never goes to the cinema, and her brother usually goes.
Nadia sometimes goes to the cinema on Friday, and her brother always goes.
Nadia usually goes to the cinema on Friday, and her brother never goes.

questions.explanation: Every Friday means every single time, which is always, and one time a year is not often, which is sometimes. The word "usually" would mean most Fridays but not all of them, and "never" would mean not one single time, so it cannot describe a brother who goes once a year.
